why: The code works for typical two-word names but has a bug in the firstName function and test gaps.

findings.title: firstName returns the second word, not the first
findings.body: The function `firstName` returns `name.trim().split(" ")[1]`, which is the second word. For "Ada Lovelace" it returns "Lovelace", not "Ada". This contradicts the doc comment on line 7.
findings.verified: Confirmed by tracing: trim() gives "Ada Lovelace", split(" ") gives ["Ada", "Lovelace"], [1] returns "Lovelace"
findings.suggestion:
firstName should return [0], not [1]:
return name.trim().split(" ")[0];

findings.title: Test only checks prefix, not the actual name
findings.body: The test uses `toMatch(/^Welcome back, /)` which only verifies the prefix. It should also check that the correct name appears after the prefix.

evidence.actual: The regex /^Welcome back, / would match any name

findings.title: No handling for single-word names
findings.body: If firstName receives a name with no space (e.g., "Madonna"), split(" ")[1] returns undefined, resulting in "Welcome back, !"

pre_merge.detail: Add welcomeBack greeting for returning users

walkthrough: Added `firstName(name)` helper that extracts a name component
Added `welcomeBack(name)` that uses firstName for informal greetings
Added test for welcomeBack that checks prefix only
